name: air_intercept_climb_toward_a_high_ball
description: The car is airborne at z 300 climbing at 1000 uu/s straight under a ball at z 1100 (no boost; both fall at the same gravity, so the gap closes at 1000 uu/s, from 800 uu). In 8 steps (0.53 s) the gap is 267 uu with the car at z about 741 and the ball at about 1008. Hand calc (independent script): Phi 0.1975 at the start, 0.4505 at step 8; sum = gamma * Phi(8) - Phi(0) plus the small leak = about +0.243 (about +18 at weight 75). The touch comes after step 9, so frames 1-8 are the approach only. The ball starts with a 1 uu/s upward velocity on purpose: in the engine a ball set with EXACTLY zero velocity in the air does not fall (it floats, measured), while any nonzero velocity makes it fall normally. Training's state setters all give the ball a random nonzero velocity.

expect.intent: climbing toward a high ball pays the potential difference, about +0.24
about +18 at weight 75 for a 0.5 s climb
the grounded orange car (carFrac about 0) earns nothing, under 5e-5
